title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. The note is in the 'équation des lacets' manuscript, the continuation of La Longue Marche. X is P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, the space underlying M_{0,4}, viewed as a double of the sphere. It is acted on by S_3 (anharmonic group) together with the antiholomorphic involution τ (complex conjugation), giving the groupoid G. The map f: X → Y is the degree-6 quotient map. Y carries orbifold points over 1/2 (with -1 and 2) of order 2 and over -j̄ = e^{iπ/3} (with -j) of order 3. The Z/2 records the real structure.

On the previous page Grothendieck chose three paths λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞ from a base point x to the points z_0, z_1, z_∞ above y. These points are g_i x with g_0 = σ̇_∞τ̇, g_1 = σ̇_0τ̇, g_∞ = τ̇. The pairs (g_i, λ_i) in π_1(X, G; x) map to the involutive generators τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞ of the extended orbifold group π_1(Y, d_Y, Z/2; y). He then rebased to the usual base point P = -j̄ by a path l from P to x. The rebased paths are λ'_i = g_i(l^{-1}) ∘ λ_i ∘ l, each running from P to g_i P.

This page computes their homotopy classes in U_{0,3}:
- λ'_0 = (σ_∞τ)(l^{-1})·λ_0·l is homotopic to the trivial loop. P lies on the fixed geodesic of the antiholomorphic reflection σ_∞τ, namely the line Re z = 1/2 through ∞, -j̄, 1/2, -j.
- λ'_1 = σ_0τ(l^{-1})·λ_1·l is likewise homotopic to the trivial loop. P lies on the fixed circle |z-1| = 1 of σ_0τ, through 0, -j̄, 2, -j.
- λ'_∞ = τ(l^{-1})·λ_∞·l is homotopic to the arc of the great circle (-j̄, 1/2, -j) from P to τP = -j.

The crossed-out opening paragraph is an earlier version of the choice of z_i. They were to be chosen as the points with f(z) = -j in the spherical triangles (1/2, j̄, 1), (-j̄, 0, -1), (0, 1/2, -j).

Purpose: the next page translates these into τ'_0 = σ̃_∞, τ'_1 = σ̃_0, τ'_∞ = τ_∞. It then verifies the Coxeter relations τ'^2 = 1, (τ'_0τ'_∞)^2 = 1, (τ'_1τ'_0)^3 = 1. These present the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group, i.e. the 'real' version of PSL_2(Z) ≅ π_1^{orb}(M_{0,4}/S_3). The compatibility of this presentation with the presentation of π_1(M_{0,3}) is checked by hand, as a step in setting up the loop equation with complex conjugation.
errors: The previous page writes τ'_0 = (σ̇_0τ̇, λ_0) and τ'_1 = (σ̇_1τ, λ_1). These are inconsistent with g_0 = σ̇_∞τ̇ and g_1 = σ̇_0τ̇. This page (and the next) correctly use σ_∞τ for λ'_0 and σ_0τ for λ'_1.
The general formula λ'_i = (…)(l^{-1})(λ_i) l has the group element left illegible/overwritten; it should read g_i(l^{-1})∘λ_i∘l.
Minor: in the λ'_∞ note the image reads 'de P = -j̄ vers τP = -j'; the transcription drops the minus sign.

ideas.what: Rebasing generators of an orbifold fundamental group with antiholomorphic elements (extended groupoid π_1(X,G)) along a path, and computing the rebased paths via fixed geodesics of reflections
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/stack fundamental group of [X/(S_3×Z/2)], real (Gal(C/R)-equivariant) fundamental groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Thurston orbifolds; real algebraic geometry); in the GT context, Drinfeld and Ihara for complex conjugation
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) discusses Teichmüller groupoids; the Z/2 extension is in this unpublished continuation

ideas.what: Presentation of the extended modular group as a Coxeter (2,3,∞) group generated by three reflections τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2(Z) as the Coxeter triangle group (2,3,∞)

missed.claim: Part of a systematic hand-built set-up of the Teichmüller groupoid in genus 0 with the real structure (complex conjugation) included as part of the discrete data. The aim is to state the 'équation des lacets' for the extended group. This is only partly paralleled in the published GT literature (real/complex-conjugation versions of GT relations).
missed.quote: λ'_∞ = (τ(l^{-1}))·λ_∞∘l homotope au lacet du grand cercle (-j̄,1/2,-j) de P = -j̄ vers τP = -j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Interesting only as documentation of how Grothendieck incorporated Gal(C/R) into the tower. The mathematics on this page is a routine check.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping: rebasing paths and identifying their homotopy classes to match a known Coxeter presentation of the extended modular group. Historically mildly interesting but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: λ'_∞ line: 'de P = -j̄ vers τP = -j' (minus sign present in the image).
The annotation under λ'_0 reads roughly 'symétrie p.r. au géod. (lune (∞,-j̄,1/2,-j))'; the crossed-out word is likely 'plan'.
The annotation under λ'_1 reads 'symétrie p.r. à l'équateur (0,-j̄,2,-j)', i.e. the circle |z-1| = 1.
The general formula reads λ'_i = (g_i)(l^{-1})(λ_i) l, with the first factor overwritten.
